correctness.boundaries: n>=3, k>=1, independent source-to-target 2-step reachable quasi-kernels only.
critical_steps: Cubic Newton sum and trig sign changes
correctness.rationale: The directed reachability and independence requirements force a nonempty cyclic core with gaps precisely 2 or 3, and pendant states are exactly optional at the first omitted vertex and mandatory at the second omitted vertex of each 3-gap. Double-counted rooted cyclic compositions yield the claimed polynomial. Newton sums of the cubic t^3-t-q, an imaginary substitution and alternating sign phases prove exactly deg(F_n) simple negative roots, avoiding inference from finite checks. Transformed factors give k=1 all real, k>=3 too few real roots, and k=2 a factor with c<=3<27/4. Direct independent brute-force checks cover 14 parameter pairs and 1,767,232 vertex subsets; exact Stirling/Sturm checks separately corroborate sampled cases. No unproved infinite inference is used.

residual_risks: Historical priority cannot be guaranteed against unindexed, non-English, or inaccessible sources.

value.rationale: Outward pendant amplification is an explicit natural construction in the motivating 2026 extremal quasi-kernel proof. An all-cardinality enumerator answers materially more than the minimum bound, and its unexpected sharp k=1/k>=2 root transition supplies an infinite-family structural obstruction to real-rootedness with a precise list of four exceptions. The result motivates the role of pendant multiplicity in quasi-kernel coefficient geometry, rather than an arbitrary tiny finite computation.
